why.why: It addresses a deeply relatable, everyday insecurity using simple animation to explain the surprising underlying auditory psychology.

hook_patterns: Counter-intuitive self-bias: framing a psychological quirk as a bizarre decision the viewer unknowingly makes.
Social defense tactics: opening with a tense, high-stakes interpersonal confrontation.
Relatable sensory glitches: highlighting a universal, daily cringe moment and promising a science-backed explanation.
todays_angle: Focus on extreme counter-intuitive cognitive traps by having Mia test Leo with a absurd real-world psychological dilemma.
ideas: Leo falls for the 'Peak-End Rule' by willingly extending a painful workout just because the last 10 seconds were easy, while Mia breaks down why his brain betrayed him.
Mia uses 'Tactical Empathy' during an argument over the last slice of pizza, completely disarming a hyper-defensive Leo in under 5 seconds.
Leo freaks out over hearing his recorded voice on a podcast, prompting Mia to physically animate bone conduction vs. air conduction inside his brain.
avoid: Generic 'Never trust a cheap...' slapstick routines that lack a core psychological explanation.
Historical trivia stories about airports or potatoes that don't fit a character-driven dynamic.
